nodes.label: PIR Camera Night Flock Frame (2022-02-27 23:43:07)
nodes.description: Overhead CCTV still from a commercial broiler house, captured by the camera channel labelled '1080P-IPC-PIR' at 2022-02-27 23:43:07. Several hundred white broilers of intermediate size are spread across a bare earth/litter floor. A suspended grey feed-conveyor pipe runs diagonally across the frame with five red-topped tube pan feeders hanging from it; birds ring the pans in dense clusters while the open floor areas hold more loosely scattered, mostly sitting birds. A red drinker bell is visible bottom-left and a glowing orange heat source (brooder/heater vent) sits at the right edge. This is a raw training/inference frame for chicken behaviour analysis, not a chart or UI.

nodes.label: Brooder Heat Source / Glowing Heater Vent
nodes.description: A bright orange glowing element at the right edge of the PIR-camera frames, consistent with a gas brooder / heater flame port in the poultry house wall. It is a fixed bright region that saturates the sensor and creates a persistent hotspot, which matters for detection models because it is a static high-contrast distractor that never moves between frames.
nodes.rationale: Heat sources are a known confounder in poultry CCTV analytics: they cause local overexposure and thermal-glow artefacts that a naive motion or brightness-based detector can mistake for activity, so behaviour models must either mask this region or rely on appearance-based detection.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-PIR Camera Channel
nodes.description: One of at least three named 1080p IP camera channels in the dataset, burned into the top-left of the frame as '1080P-IPC-PIR'. This channel views the pen from a shallower, more oblique angle than the others and includes the heater wall and a red bell drinker in view.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Camera-Label Overlay
nodes.description: Every frame in this chunk carries a top-right date-time stamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) and a top-left camera identifier. Together these give each still an implicit (camera, timestamp) key, which is what allows frames to be ordered into behaviour sequences and grouped by bird age and time-of-day without any separate metadata file.
nodes.rationale: The overlay is the only source of provenance for these stills, so it doubles as the dataset's de-facto index; it is also a fixed white-on-dark region that should be cropped or masked before training so the model does not key on rendered digits.

nodes.label: Elevated Overhead Wide-Angle Viewpoint
nodes.description: All frames are shot from a ceiling-mounted wide-angle lens looking down and across the pen, producing visible barrel distortion (the floor cable and pen edge bow into arcs) and a strong scale gradient: birds near the top of the frame are much smaller in pixels than birds at the bottom. Individuals appear as top-down feathered ovals with no visible head-on silhouette.
nodes.rationale: The top-down view is chosen because it minimises occlusion between densely stocked birds and gives near-complete pen coverage from one camera, at the cost of losing the side profile cues (posture, leg extension) that a ground-level camera would give — so behaviour must be inferred from footprint shape, spacing and motion rather than pose.
